note: Verified 2026-08-05: 14 companies. The Wine Industry Network supplier directory alone produced 10 of them; the full 6,127-company YC crawl produced almost nothing. Industry-specific directories beat general startup databases for a vertical radar, the same way trade shows beat cloud marketplaces. 4 of 14 made a real AI claim, the rest were honest none entries. 2026-08-29: 7 finds. NEW BEST AU/NZ SOURCE: winetitles.com.au/supplier-category/<slug>/ is fully server-rendered across 122 categories. Wine Industry Network has gone CLIENT-rendered (the old search?keyword= no longer answers curl) and is largely mined out. brewingindustryguide.com/suppliers yielded 2 hits across all 26 pages with roughly half its software listings on dead domains: treat as exhausted. 2026-09-15: 2 new (Claret, EOSYS). NOW robots-disallowed for ClaudeBot, do not attempt: winetitles.com.au (was best AU/NZ source), scotchwhisky.com suppliers, SIBA, distilling.com, craftbrewingbusiness.com. WineBusiness buyer's guide moved to POST https://wbbuyersguide.com/api/ ({apiFunc:getVendors,prodLevel:prodDetail,prodId:473} BI, 480 ERP; getProfile by profileId). Brewers Association supplier list is member-login only. 2026-09-21: 11 finds on ZERO searches, and the wbbuyersguide API is much richer than the note above said. It is a full machine-readable catalogue, not just two prodIds. Three facts worth keeping: (1) apiFunc getAutoComplete with {"q":"<term>"} returns matching CATEGORIES with prodId and tier, which is how to enumerate the taxonomy; a 40-term sweep surfaced 176 categories. (2) getVendors takes prodLevel "prodProduct" or "prodDetail", NOT "product", so whole product-level categories pull at once: 311 Industry Data, 312 Wine Production Software, 313 Vineyard Software, 308 Drones, 325 Winery DTC Technology, 265 Weather Monitoring, 260 Soil Testing, 179 Control Systems. (3) getProfile with {"profileId":N} returns the vendor website domain and city/country directly, removing the guesswork step. Not bot-walled, answers every request with a browser UA. BACKLOG: only 25 of 176 categories were pulled, giving 276 vendors of which 187 are NOT tracked. Categories still unpulled include labs 203 and 224, bottling QC 425, optical sorting 550 beyond what was taken, and consultants 278. This is the single biggest known unworked seam in the radar; budget a dedicated scout for it. Big Idea Ventures now 403s both wp-json/wp/v2/company and /portfolio, so the older note on it is stale. CorkVision, Vintality, ePlant and Central UAS Technologies have live directory listings but broken sites (parked redirect, timeout, TLS handshake failure, expired cert) and need a browser pass.

label: RAG and LLM knowledge solution providers for beverage
hint: Vendors and integrators building retrieval-augmented generation, LLM copilots, document/knowledge assistants or semantic search over beverage industry data: brewing SOPs and batch records, QA/QC and food-safety documentation, HACCP, distillery and winery compliance (TTB, excise, label approval), technical libraries (MBAA, IBD, ASBC, AWRI, OIV), supplier spec sheets and CoAs, sensory panel notes, tasting notes and wine/whisky catalogues, sales-rep and distributor copilots for beverage route to market. Look for named beverage or food-and-beverage customers and case studies, not generic 'chat with your PDF' startups. Include LLM/RAG platform vendors ONLY where a beverage, brewing, distilling, winery or food-and-beverage manufacturing customer or use case is named on their own site.
note: New surface (2026-08-11). Highest signal: vendor case-study pages naming a brewery, distillery, winery or drinks group; food-and-beverage manufacturing RAG copilots; wine/spirits retail and sommelier recommendation assistants where the vendor sells the tech. Beware AI-written listicles of 'best RAG tools' - they are a known contamination source and are not a second source. 2026-08-29: 6 finds. label: Brewing and distilling institutes, professional bodies and schools
hint: probrewer.com (supplier directory and forums); MBAA mbaa.com (technical committees, district meetings, Technical Quarterly, Master Brewers Podcast); Brewers Association brewersassociation.org (CBC seminar programmes, Brewers Publications, technical committees); IBD ibd.org.uk (Journal of the Institute of Brewing, Brewer and Distiller International, member and corporate member directory); ICBD at Heriot-Watt (research group, PhD projects, industry partners); TUM Weihenstephan (Chair of Brewing and Beverage Technology, Lehrstuhl research pages, spin-outs); also VLB Berlin, Doemens, Siebel Institute, Campden BRI, ASBC, EBC and Brewers of Europe, World Brewing Congress, UC Davis viticulture and enology, AWRI, SWRI, OIV. Two jobs: (a) the institute, chair or research group itself when it runs real AI, ML or data work on beer, whisky or wine, and (b) its proceedings, conference programmes, sponsor lists, spin-outs and corporate member directories as a route to companies.
note: New surface added 2026-09-21 at Ankur's request, never swept before, so treat every route as unproven and record what worked in this note. Highest-value targets are university spin-outs and named research groups: TUM Weihenstephan and ICBD both publish project and staff pages. Conference programmes (World Brewing Congress, MBAA district meetings, CBC seminars, EBC congress) name both vendors and academics doing ML work and are usually server-rendered HTML or PDF. An academic chair is only an entry when the AI work is its own and named; a university teaching brewing is not a finding. Check robots.txt before crawling any of these: mapyourshow.com hosts CBC and disallows us. FIRST SWEEP RESULT 2026-09-21: 4 finds (TUM Chair of Brewing and Beverage Technology, Weihenstephan Standards, Julius Kuehn Institute Geilweilerhof, Campden BRI) plus a browser pass that recovered the best one, the University of Melbourne Digital Agriculture, Food and Wine group. label: Academic literature and research papers on AI in brewing, distilling and wine
hint: Peer-reviewed papers, preprints and conference proceedings where AI, machine learning, computer vision, spectroscopy chemometrics or predictive modelling is applied to beer, whisky, wine, malt, hops, yeast, fermentation, sensory or packaging. Work the FREE scholarly APIs, which need no search engine: OpenAlex (api.openalex.org/works?filter=title_and_abstract.search:...), Crossref (api.crossref.org/works?query=...), arXiv (export.arxiv.org/api/query), Semantic Scholar (api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/search), Europe PMC, DOAJ and MDPI. Key journals: Journal of the Institute of Brewing, MBAA Technical Quarterly, ASBC Journal, Food Chemistry, Food Control, Journal of Food Engineering, Fermentation (MDPI), Beverages (MDPI), OENO One, Australian Journal of Grape and Wine Research, Computers and Electronics in Agriculture. The FINDING is never the paper itself: it is the company, spin-out, institute research group or named industrial collaborator behind it. Mine author affiliations, funding and acknowledgements statements, and 'data availability' or 'conflict of interest' declarations, which is where the industrial partner is usually named.
note: New surface added 2026-09-21. It exists to fix a recorded weakness: the store has ZERO papers, videos or podcasts among its source URLs, so the two-source rule is only genuinely independent for about half the entries. This surface has two outputs. First, NEW companies found through author affiliations and industrial collaborators. Second, and just as valuable, a PAPER AS AN INDEPENDENT SECOND SOURCE for companies already tracked: list those separately under an 'enrichments' array giving the company name or domain and the paper URL plus DOI. Remember the merge gate needs one source on the entry's own domain, so a paper can only ever be the second source, never the first. Academic authors are private individuals: never write a claim about a named person, and never set company_is_current. Prefer a DOI or publisher landing page over a PDF mirror or ResearchGate.

label: Generative AI adopted BY beer, whisky and wine companies themselves
hint: The OPERATOR side of generative AI, not vendors selling it (the 'rag' surface already covers vendors). Brewers, distillers, wineries, drinks groups, distributors and retailers running LLMs, copilots, agents, diffusion models or foundation models in their own business. Use cases: generative recipe and flavour design, LLM copilots over brewing or batch data, RAG over SOPs and technical libraries, AI-generated label art and marketing copy, sensory and tasting-note generation, sommelier and beer-finder chatbots, demand forecasting on foundation models, agentic procurement, vision-language models on packaging lines, GenAI in customer service and trade marketing. Named targets worth checking: AB InBev, Heineken, Carlsberg, Molson Coors, Asahi, Kirin, Suntory, Sapporo, Tsingtao, Diageo, Pernod Ricard, Bacardi, Brown-Forman, Beam Suntory, William Grant, Edrington, Constellation Brands, Treasury Wine Estates, Concha y Toro, E&J Gallo, Accolade, Moet Hennessy, Thai Bev, United Breweries, Kingfisher, Bira 91, Radico Khaitan, Allied Blenders. ROUTES: company newsrooms and press releases, annual and ESG reports, investor day decks, CAREERS PAGES (a brewer hiring a GenAI or LLM engineer is evidence in itself), and the customer-story pages of the foundation-model and data vendors: openai.com/index and /customer-stories, anthropic.com/customers, databricks.com/customers, snowflake.com/customers, mistral.ai, cohere.com, huggingface.co, nvidia.com industry pages.
note: New surface added 2026-09-21 at Ankur's request, never swept before. The distinction from 'rag' is who owns the AI: rag is vendors selling into beverage, genai is the drinks company doing it itself. Many of the big operators are ALREADY tracked, so for those the output is an evidence refresh or a GenAI capability detail, not a new row: put those in the enrichments file rather than forcing a duplicate. GenAI is the most over-claimed category in the industry, so the no-inflation rule bites hardest here: a press release about 'AI-powered marketing' with no named system, no partner and no deployment detail is marketing, and belongs nowhere. A careers posting is good evidence of intent but is NOT evidence of a shipped system: grade it 'exploring' at most. Practitioner forums are a lead source only, never a source: see the Reddit note in the skill.

label: Pooled operational benchmarking clubs and peer data consortia for drinks
hint: A business model, not a product category: many producers submit their own plant, cost or sustainability data, an operator validates and anonymises it, and members get their performance ranked against peers. The template is the NIRAS Brewing Benchmark Club (NBBC), where hundreds of breweries benchmark packaging OEE split by glass returnable, glass non-returnable, can, keg and PET, plus production KPIs for water, electricity and heat consumption, extract loss, productivity and brewery utilisation. Look for: brewery and distillery operational benchmarking clubs; winery and vineyard FINANCIAL benchmarking (Moss Adams and Silicon Valley Bank both publish annual wine industry benchmarks, Wine Business Institute at Sonoma State, Vinpro in South Africa, Turrentine); sustainability and utility benchmarking consortia (Beverage Industry Environmental Roundtable, Carbon Trust, CDP, Water Footprint Network); association benchmarking surveys (Brewers Association brewery operations benchmarking, MBAA, Campden BRI, VLB Berlin, Doemens, AWRI, Wine Australia); cross-industry benchmarking firms with a drinks practice (Solomon Associates class); and brewery consultancies that run a recurring multi-client data set rather than one-off projects (First Key Consulting class). Agronomic peer-comparison networks for barley, hops and grapes count too.
note: New surface added 2026-09-21 at Ankur's request, prompted by the NIRAS NBBC page, never swept before. NIRAS itself is ALREADY TRACKED under the engineering surface, so it is the template, not a find. SCOPE BOUNDARIES, read before working: this is NOT the 'engineering' surface (consultancies and historians) and NOT 'marketdata' (NielsenIQ, Circana, IWSR and other sales and consumer measurement). The test is whether MEMBERS CONTRIBUTE THEIR OWN DATA into a pooled, anonymised set they then get compared against. A consultancy that merely writes reports is out. A market research firm buying scanner data is out. Most of these will have NO machine learning at all, which is fine and expected: they are pooled data assets and they matter to the beverage data landscape, so enter them honestly with ai_maturity 'none'. This directly targets the Consulting theme, one of the two weakest slices of the radar. Many of these bodies publish only a PDF report, so check whether a real recurring member data set sits behind it before entering; a one-off industry survey is not a benchmarking club.
